svg.text: BEST FOR: OAUTH 2.0 + PKCE VS. OIDC + AGENT OBO
FORMAT LINEAGE: Alex Xu / ByteByteGo (#07) & Shalini Goyal (#06) • RFC 8693 Agent Identity
OAuth 2.0 + PKCE vs. OpenID Connect (OIDC) + RFC 8693 Agent Delegation: The Protocol Sequence Diff
OAuth 2.0 grants delegated API permission; OIDC proves user identity; RFC 8693 'act' claims bind an AI agent to the human it acts for.
PANEL A • OAUTH 2.0 AUTHORIZATION CODE + PKCE (DELEGATED PERMISSION — NOT IDENTITY)
Prompt user login & scope consent screen
Call MCP / API with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
• Answers 'What is this app allowed to access?' — never use
an opaque access_token as proof of who logged in.
• PKCE (RFC 7636) binds the authorization code to the exact
client that started the flow via code_verifier.
• Scope ceiling: the access_token only carries the consented
PANEL B • OPENID CONNECT (OIDC) + RFC 8693 ON-BEHALF-OF (OBO) AGENT DELEGATION
Sign in with OIDC (scope=openid profile email)
Issue signed id_token (JWT proving user identity) + access_token
Verify id_token signature, iss, aud, exp (sub = 'alice@corp')
Mint narrowed OBO JWT with both sub='alice' and act={'sub':'agent'}
tools/call with Bearer <OBO_JWT> (5-min TTL, single-task scope)
OPA verifies BOTH alice's RBAC and agent's allowlist -> execute & log
• OIDC adds the signed id_token so the app knows *who* the
• Never give an agent a god-mode service account! Exchange
the user token via RFC 8693 for a narrowed OBO token.
• Downstream tools authorize the intersection of (Human User
RBAC ∩ Agent Capability Policy) and log both IDs.
OIDC + RFC 8693 Agent OBO JWT (Dual Identity)
Rule: OAuth 2.0 authorizes APIs; OIDC authenticates humans; RFC 8693 'act' tokens ensure an AI agent never exceeds the human's permissions.
Curated by Nitin Aggarwal • Google Cloud ADK + OpenHands Factory • Proprietary + Confidential
Alex Xu / ByteByteGo, 'OAuth 2.0 vs OIDC' (#07) • Shalini Goyal (#06) • RFC 6749 / RFC 7636 (PKCE) / OIDC Core / RFC 8693 Token Exchange
